The answer declares the bible exception openly, keeps the engine laws, and delivers slow motion, saturated green, the white dress, the smile and a distant solo accordion with an anti-forró fence. Glow and bloom are allowed. The house style shows up mainly as grime and an invented motive, neither of which works against the brief.

contradictions: Spatial geometry conflicts: 'the camera stays on the sea side of the AVO–NETO line' while GEOMETRY puts 'the sea's edge 10 m to frame-right' and the wides show 'the sea and the sun in the gap between them'. With the camera on the sea side, the sea would be behind the camera, not in frame-right or between them

Lock 4: 'The low sun stays ... behind the boy', but the boy faces frame-left toward the grandfather, so the sun is behind him and both faces are rim-lit only. Workable, but SHOT 3's MCU of @AVO 'from @NETO's side' places the camera roughly into the sun
probes.notes: Realist rigour is intact, with no regression. Both characters get full acting tasks with living eyes. Physics is specific (cord springs back, a knot seats only under a hard pull, the net drags, sand clings). There is one named light source (low sun frame-right) with sky fill and a ban on frontal or beauty light. The music ban uses synonyms. Five locks, a voice lock with a Ceará accent, references with one job each, and a 35mm/MEGA-REAL look. The only weakness is a real axis and sea-side geometry inconsistency, plus a ~2,000-word length that the notes flag as over the official guidance.

judges.overall: After the change, the skill mostly serves the brief rather than its own aesthetic. All five non-realist briefs got the style they asked for: saturated neon with a rig orbit, pastel high-key with a locked tripod, a saturated slow-motion dream with an accordion, epic fantasy with glow and a crane, and stepped claymation with a score. In each case the realist defaults (handheld, music ban, no flares, grain) were explicitly turned off. The house style that remains is structural and verbal, not visual. Every output carries the full ACTING ladder and LIVING EYES physiology (most harmful in p2, where it fights 'sem expressão'), the 'If any surface looks clean — WRONG' or OVER-REAL grime clause (p3, p4, p5), 'shadows breathing / NO vignette' boilerplate, invented motives in THE SOUL lines (p1, p4), and the compulsory hard cut mid-action (p1, p2, p5) even where a clip, jingle or gag would want a resolved ending. Craft errors are mostly self-contradictions: p2's top-down insert breaks its own frontal-shot lock and the brief's 'frontal' cuts, p5's camera height doesn't match the mouse's eye height, p4's lightning versus 'even exposure', and in r1 the camera is on the sea side yet the sea is in frame. The r1 control shows no loss of realist rigour: full acting tasks, specific physics, a single motivated sun source, a music ban with synonyms, and five clear locks all hold. The skill's own notes are candid about the remaining pulls, which points to the department templates (performance, realism, story endings) as the next places to make style-conditional.

"LIVING EYES: ... involuntary detail"
"Hard end mid-pose" with music "cuts dead at 10s" on a cheerful gag
"NEVER looks into the lens" (claymation gags often play to camera)
contradictions: NOT "cartoon-squash-and-stretch exaggeration" vs SOUND "cartoonish pops", squeaky 'boing' and clay that "squashes and flattens on landing" (mild tension)
probes.notes: Most medium-native answer: animated on twos (12 poses/s), locked tripod as real stop-motion idiom, cotton-wool steam on wire, cellophane flame, clay 'boiling', blinks as eyelid replacements, fingerprint whorls - concrete, surprising, engine-aware (negatives against interpolation/motion blur, draft check for fluid motion). Music cue holds a suspended note on the throw and resolves on landing. Over-structured acting and the forced hard-cut ending are the only house residue.

contradictions: Camera kept "on the sea side of the AVO–NETO line" yet the sea and sun are "frame-right" behind the boy ("the sea's edge 10 m to frame-right") - if the camera were on the sea side, the sea/sun would be behind the camera, not in frame
CONTRACT "handheld... breathes" while every shot "STAYS PUT" - deliberate softening, not a contradiction per se
probes.notes: No loss of realist rigor: full acting tasks for both (test the work not the boy; steal glances at hands), knot physics with resistance and a self-mending-net lock, single named light source (low sun ~3000 K + 7500 K sky fill, long shadows), exhaustive music ban with synonyms, one-line dialogue lock with accent and VOICE LOCK, reference scoping (jangada object-only), Higgsfield token note, child-face provider warning. Directorial idea (affection shown only by letting go silently, eyes already on the sea) is specific. Only real flaw is the axis/sun geometry inconsistency and ~2,000-word length.

judges.overall: Across the five off-style briefs, the skill now honors the requested aesthetic in the parts that matter most: saturated neon and orbit (p1), a locked, symmetrical high-key frame (p2), slow motion and saturated green with a declared exception to the bible (p3), magic glow and a crane (p4), and stepped claymation (p5). The best answers, p3 and p5, make directorial choices that are specific to the medium and aware of what the engine can do: the gaze inversion in the dream, and stop-motion animated on twos with practical-effect steam. The remaining house style is structural rather than aesthetic. Every answer carries the arthouse acting ladder ("the work happens in the eyes", LIVING EYES, involuntary details), a material-grime mandate ("If any surface looks clean… WRONG"), "hard end mid-X" endings, and an "even exposure, NO vignette" boilerplate. This residue undercuts deadpan comedy (p2) and epic grandeur (p4). It also creates small internal contradictions: lock wording copied from the template that clashes with the shot lists (p2, p4), and a mouth-versus-nose breath conflict in p1. The regression case r1 keeps full realist rigor (acting tasks, knot physics, a single sun source, the music ban, locks and reference scoping). Its one real defect is a camera-axis versus sun/sea geometry inconsistency. Net: style fidelity is good. Creativity is strongest where the brief invites conceptual inversion. Craft loses points for template boilerplate that is not adapted to non-realist genres.
